questions.question: How often is your documented information security policy, approved by senior management, reviewed?
questions.guidance: State approval authority, current version and date of last review.
questions.evidence: Approved policy document showing version, approver and review date
questions.delivery_models: Vendor-hosted; Client-hosted (all tiers); Staff in client environment (all tiers)
questions.benchmark: At least annually.

questions.question: Is there a named executive accountable for information security (CISO or equivalent) independent of IT delivery?
questions.guidance: Provide name, title, reporting line and date appointed.
questions.evidence: Organisation chart or appointment letter

questions.question: Do you operate a documented information security risk assessment methodology with a maintained risk register?
questions.guidance: Confirm assessment frequency and how risks affecting client services are treated.
questions.evidence: Risk methodology and extract of current risk register

questions.question: Does your certified or documented ISMS scope explicitly cover the people, processes and systems used to deliver this service to <Client>?

questions.evidence: ISMS scope statement or certificate scope page

questions.question: Is cyber and information security risk reported to the board or an equivalent governing body, and how frequently?

questions.evidence: Committee terms of reference and redacted minutes or reporting pack

questions.question: Do you maintain a register of statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations relevant to this service?

questions.benchmark: For an Indian client, expect the register to cover the Indian financial-sector rules that apply (for example RBI, SEBI or IRDAI) and the DPDP Act.

questions.evidence: Firewall rule review record

questions.evidence: Hosting and region declaration for the in-scope service

questions.guidance: Provide the responsibility split for identity, encryption, backup and monitoring.

questions.question: Are technical controls in place to ensure <Client> data and logs are stored and processed only in permitted locations, including in-country only where <Client>'s regulation requires it?

module_triggers.include_when: The service can create, change or approve payments, orders, trades, holdings or client-asset records.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Can the service affect payments, trades or client assets?" → Yes

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor hosts, operates or stores anything for the client on cloud or vendor-controlled infrastructure.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Where does the service run?" → Vendor-hosted or cloud
module_triggers.note: Renamed from "Cloud & Hosting" in bank version 3, to tell it apart from the base domain "Cloud & Hosting Security"

module_triggers.include_when: Vendor staff hold production, database, admin or security-tool access.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Access to client systems" → Privileged or admin

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor receives, stores or can access personal data, including employee data.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Data the vendor handles" → Personal data or higher

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor develops, supplies, deploys or maintains software or APIs the client uses.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Does the vendor supply software or APIs?" → Yes

module_triggers.include_when: Client data sits at vendor or subcontractor facilities, or vendor staff work on client premises.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Client data at vendor sites, or vendor staff on client premises?" → Yes

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor supplies software that is installed and run in the client's own environment (the vendor does not host it).
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "How is the service delivered?" → Software installed in the client's environment. Also switches the Base set to rows tagged Client-hosted.

module_triggers.include_when: DRAFT: vendor developers or other staff work inside the client's environment (client devices, virtual desktops, repositories).
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "How is the service delivered?" → Vendor staff work inside the client's environment. Base set becomes the 8 rows tagged Staff in client environment.

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor answers Yes to AIS-01 (AI will be used to provide the scoped services), or the consultant adds it.
module_triggers.trigger: Vendor answer to AIS-01 = Yes. AIM-08 = Yes raises the tier to at least High. A later model or provider change triggers an early reassessment.

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor provides a service that is not technology: facilities, housekeeping, security guards, staffing, couriers, call centres, printing, consultants.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "How is the service delivered?" → Non-technology service. Base set becomes the 17 rows tagged Non-technology services, for every tier; add the Personal Data module if the vendor handles personal data.
